palette.use: ice-cream truck body, interior walls, candy pillars
interior glow, pink light wash, candy lamp shades
caption text, window lights, streetlamps, neon clock
picket fence, character skin, truck door burst of light

color_arc: Starts cool blue-dusk exteriors (frames 1-5, muted navy/gray street) → explodes into saturated hot-pink/magenta interior (frames 6-9, 10) → snaps back to cold blue night exterior for 'vanished' → ends in alarming deep-red/black neon clock frame ('exactly'). Emotional arc: calm → seductive/pink → ominous red.
caption_style: Rounded bold sans (Comic-Sans-adjacent/rounded display like Baloo or Fredoka), warm yellow #FFE84D with thin dark brown/black outline (~2-3px) and slight soft drop shadow; caption height ≈ 5-7% of frame height; positioned bottom-center or center-bottom third, NEVER at very edge; ONE word per frame (occasionally two: 'ice-cream' style compound), reading as a word-per-shot chant across the sheet; implied animation = word pops in with the cut, possibly tiny scale-up bounce.
character_staging: Mix of scales: 1-2 wide establishing shots (truck on road, interior POV), several medium shots (character walking by fence), and 1 tight close-up (face fills ~60% of frame height, frame 3). Characters are blocky/simple = strong silhouettes: blue-jacket protagonist reads instantly. Facing: truck head-on then rear; protagonist faces camera in close-up, 3/4 back walking away in 'vanished'; interior crowd faces away/toward glow. Never more than 2-3 characters per frame; interior crowds are glowing featureless silhouettes.
camera: Frames 1-2 imply a slow push-in on the parked truck (closer each cut); frame 3 hard cut to close-up (crash-in); frames 6-9 alternate POV shots implying forward dolly through interior; frame 10 slight low-angle push toward protagonist; frame 12 static or slow push on the clock. Overall: cut-driven push-in rhythm, no pans or handheld.
lighting: Night scene lit by discrete glowing sources: warm streetlamps, truck's own pink-white interior glow (bloom/halo blowout on door frame 6), candy lamps casting pink wash. Contrast is high: dark navy surroundings vs hot pink/white light pools. Interior frames are nearly blown-out pink with soft bloom everywhere; final frame is a red neon glow on dark. No daylight, no ambient soft light.
huss_treatment: No explicit 'HUSS' caption appears; closest analog is the one-word chant captions ('music', 'broke', 'driving', 'the', 'door', 'children', 'bite', 'again', 'vanished', 'exactly') — single word, uniform yellow-outlined style, same position every frame, 1 word = 1 cut, acting as rhythm. If adding a chant word: same yellow, same size, no distortion, no repetition within a frame.
empty_vs_dense: Exterior frames ~60-70% empty (flat navy sky and dark road dominate; 3-4 props only). Interior frames ~80% dense-but-soft: pink glow fills space, repeated candy-pillar/lamp motifs, but detail is low-frequency (big shapes, not clutter). Rule: outside = empty and moody, inside = flooded with one color.
the_5_things: 1. One-word yellow rounded caption with dark outline, same position every shot — the entire narration is carried by word-per-cut rhythm.
2. Color-arc storytelling: muted navy night → overwhelming saturated pink interior → cold blue → red alarm frame; let one hue own each sequence.
3. A single glowing 'magical object' (the pink truck/door) that blows out with bloom and lights everything around it — the light source IS the story.
4. Simple high-silhouette character in one recognizable costume (blue jacket) reused across all shots for instant readability.
5. Empty-frame discipline: exteriors keep 60%+ flat sky/road so the glowing subject pops; only 3-4 props per exterior.
